# Identity upgrades must cover ACK and negative replay

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Open when message identity changes or a ledger accepts a compatibility wildcard.

Identity changes must reach negative replay and every ledger-writing path, not
just new-message admission. At F270/#322, sender-scoped indexes and specialized
enqueue/note guards passed, yet generic enqueue({}) -> claim -> ack_delivery
wrote a NEW sender_seat='' row. The legacy wildcard then collapsed a legitimate
other sender's same-id body. Test ACK after generic enqueue as well as admission,
and preserve claim state when a refused ACK rolls back.

arrive_control was another escape: it replayed terminal Refused by recipient and
msg_id only. Self's refused control could suppress the parent's own same-id
control before the new sender-scoped queue key was consulted. Prove both
same-sender refusal replay and different-sender independence.

Compatibility wildcards are one-directional brakes only while their provenance
is confined to legacy records. Enforce that invariant at the final writer.
Do not call a new wildcard harmless because another admission path is guarded.

Migration proof used the actual embedded sqlx Migrator with a deliberate error
after ledger copy and before commit. It rolled back rows, rename/rebuild,
generated column, indexes, pragma and migration success; two later opens
migrated once and quick_check was ok. No production database writes.

Cost caveat: a settled-expiry port read saves native-lock/queue-write work but
can still walk sender/kind event history; three SQL EXISTS subprobes are not
always three literal seeks because legacy/current sender keys both count.

Magic wand: a shared Queue contract for all final ledger writers plus a terminal
outcome replay identity matrix. Keep migration rollback/reopen and same/different
sender controls beside it. Read-only detached review remains C25; use exact-head
CI for TS and serialized session-local Rust/SQLite probes, never dependency links.
